recommendation: Keep the audit commit as-is. No FHIR-core follow-up is needed for FHIR-16966 unless the work group wants a separate contributor-facing policy for when new elements should choose markdown rather than string.
issue_request: FHIR-16966 was a Published/Persuasive with Modification MnM issue asking FHIR-core to use string, markdown, and xhtml consistently. The resolution established string as the default unless a markdown use case exists, limited xhtml to Narrative, and called for documenting that string-to-markdown evolution is non-breaking for non-choice elements and that adding markdown as a choice is also non-breaking.
initial_application: The issue was applied in svn revision 14160, represented in git by a5c90c3db3cc87902faf8b096c1fdc5f179853fc, which explicitly named GF#16966 in a datatype documentation batch. That commit added markdown-as-string and string-to-markdown compatibility guidance to source/datatypes.html and added a string-to-markdown compatibility exception to source/versions.html.
additional_context: Current source keeps the requested guidance in the active datatype and compatibility pages. Later final issues FHIR-38714, FHIR-40555, FHIR-51051, and the already-published FHIR-20853 reconciliation refined markdown safety, choice-element compatibility, same-domain datatype compatibility, and datatype subtype substitutability. source/fhir.ini maps datatype pages to datatypes.html and xhtml to narrative; current XML StructureDefinition source has no xhtml type code outside Narrative-oriented handling. MnM minutes from 2018-07-10 corroborate FHIR-16966 as Persuasive with Mod.
reconciliation: Published an empty audit commit because no current FHIR-core source correction is needed. The current spec already conveys the required implementer-facing rule, and adding a redundant authoring-policy sentence would be broader than necessary and could drift from later refined compatibility wording.

related_jiras.note: Same 2018 datatype batch clarified string and markdown datatype rules that support FHIR-16966's consistency decision.
Corrected markdown CommonMark/GFM and no-inline-HTML guidance while preserving the string-to-markdown compatibility note.
Refined string-to-markdown compatibility text for single-type versus choice elements and safe rendering of existing string values.
Broadened the compatibility policy from a special string-to-markdown exception to same-domain datatype changes while retaining string-to-markdown as an example.
Clarified that datatype specialization does not imply substitutability, reinforcing that markdown is only allowed where explicitly listed.
